thread:
Siva Rao: CI started failing after the paged-attn merge — link errors from nvcc when creating libflashkernels.a
Anika Patel: saw that too. Error shows `undefined reference` to fused attention entry symbols. Did we change symbol visibility or extern "C" across builds?
Benji Chen: paste from CI:
```
/usr/bin/ld: /workspace/libflashkernels.a(fused_attn.o): in function `some_wrapper':
fused_attn.o: undefined reference to `_Z18fused_attn_launcherP...
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
ci-bot: build/flash-attn-linux-cuda11.8 #238 failed in step "link flash_kernels" (exit code 2)
TJ: repro'd locally in an alpine-based runner that uses musl and gcc 10. ubuntu:22.04/gcc11 builds succeed. So toolchain/libc mismatch likely.
Maya: alpine images save size but musl/gcc differences change inlining and visibility. Could be `-fvisibility=hidden` combined with different ar/ranlib behaviour.
Siva Rao: the paged-attn packaging added a small C++ wrapper that expects C++ ABI. If somewhere we compile with D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=0, symbol names change.
Anika Patel: can someone run `nm` on the static archive artifacts in both images? need to compare mangled names.
Benji Chen: done. ubuntu build shows:
```
00000000 T _Z18fused_attn_launcherPvPiS_
```
and alpine shows the same symbol but link still fails referencing a different mangled suffix in the wrapper.
Benji Chen: additional note: nvcc emits `--compiler-bindir=/usr/bin/g++-11` warning on alpine when gcc 10 is default. That might lead to host compiler/ABI mismatch during link.
TJ: temporary workaround: build wrappers with `extern "C"` exports and `-fvisibility=default`. Verified linking then succeeds on musl.
Maya: but that is a bandaid. We saw perf drops too: canary runs from alpine-built artifacts are ~10-15% slower on fused-attn throughput vs ubuntu-built artifacts.
Anika Patel: profiling (ncu) compares: ubuntu build shows higher shared L1 reuse and lower global loads. alpine build includes extra memcpy in KV cache path during eviction — suspect libc memcpy implementation differences.
Siva Rao: that aligns with kube perf results: KV cache tail latency higher on alpine artifact. Might be due to different inline or memcpy sematics hitting kernel fallback code paths.
Benji Chen: also found different default compile flags: ubuntu CI sets -O3 and LTO disabled; alpine job had -O2 and `-fno-plt` set. Small flag diffs can pick different kernel variants at runtime.
TJ: root cause hypothesis: toolchain + flags + cuda arch selection produce different PTX/SASS outputs. fused vs flash variants chosen at runtime based on sm/ptx heuristics, causing divergent perf.
Maya: immediate plan:
- revert paged-attn packaging change that altered wrapper visibility (hotfix) — Siva will open PR
- unify CI toolchains to the perf reference: gcc 11 + glibc-based ubuntu image for core kernel builds — TJ to update CI config
- add a perf-smoke CI job that runs a fused-attn microbench and emits ncu metrics artifact so we can detect regressions early — Benji to add harness
- enforce consistent compile flags across images via shared build-config script
Anika Patel: also add `ncu --export` JSON artifact with metrics l1_shared_hit_rate,l2_read_throughput,dram_read_throughput for quick diffs.
Benji Chen: added branch perf/ci-ncu-harness with a small harness that runs fused/paged/flash variants for batch sizes [1,8,32], sequence lengths [128,512], and records mean throughput/latency.
ci-bot: artifact: https://ci.redwood.dev/artifacts/flashattn/238/ncu-smoke.json
Siva Rao: going to include `-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1` and force `-fvisibility=default` on wrapper TU in the revert PR to avoid mangling mismatches when reintroducing packaging.
TJ: long-term: document a build reference in eng-runtime runbook and add a CI gate that builds on both ubuntu & alpine images and diffs the perf artifacts (non-blocking for normal PRs).
Maya: agree. Also we should pin CUDA gencode flags (explicit sm list) rather than generic compute to avoid differing kernel selection on driver/toolchain combos.
Anika Patel: one more gotcha: musl's memcpy can use different vectorized paths; if our kernel relies on certain latency characteristics, that affects KV cache eviction heuristics. Prefer glibc for perf-critical builds.
Benji Chen: FYI: if we insist on tiny images later, consider building on ubuntu and then packaging runtime into a slim image, not compiling in musl directly.
Siva Rao: action items assigned: Siva (revert + flags), TJ (CI image/toolchain pin), Benji (perf harness + artifacts), Anika (ncu metrics + smoke test design), Maya (runbook update). ETA for revert: EOD today.
TJ: also bumped the `link` job to run `nm` checks and fail if expected exported symbols missing.
ci-bot: build/flash-attn-linux-cuda11.8 #239 queued
Maya: thanks everyone. Once revert lands, we'll run the full fused/paged/flash benchmark matrix and post diffs here.
Siva Rao: will follow up with diffed ncu JSON and a short summary comparing L1/L2 metrics and KV latency after the build alignment.
TJ: :thumbsup:
